platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI) — Codex
details: **Codex CLI 0.134.0 (May 26, 2026)**: Enhanced MCP server setup with **per-server environment targeting and OAuth capabilities**; **read-only MCP tools can now execute concurrently** when flagged; added search across local conversation history (case-insensitive content matches with previews); `--profile` flag now prioritized across CLI, permissions, and sandbox workflows; improved connector tool schema reliability; extended context for extension tools and subagent identification in hook inputs. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI
details: **Colab Enterprise — Data Science Agent, now generally available (May 26, 2026)**: A built-in agent inside Colab Enterprise notebooks that creates multi-step plans, generates and **executes code**, reasons about results, and presents findings. Spans exploratory data analysis through ML predictions/forecasts, and performs large-scale data processing using **BigQuery ML, BigQuery DataFrames, or Managed Service for Apache Spark**. Accesses data via uploaded CSV files or referenced BigQuery tables. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/colab/docs/use-data-science-agent

platforms.name: Cursor
details: **/loop Skill (Version 3.5, May 20, 2026)**: New bundled agent skill that lets an agent **run a prompt repeatedly on a local schedule until a certain outcome is achieved** (e.g., monitoring deployment status). Introduces recurring, unattended scheduled agent execution on the endpoint. Source: https://cursor.com/docs/skills

findings.title: OpenAI Codex CLI — OAuth-authenticated MCP servers + per-server environment targeting
findings.description: Codex CLI 0.134.0 adds OAuth login flows for MCP servers (server-advertised scopes, configurable callback port/URL) and **per-server environment variable targeting** (`--env KEY=VALUE`, `env_http_headers` pulling values from the environment). This is an extension of the Codex MCP connection surface: a Codex endpoint can now hold OAuth tokens for, and inject distinct secrets/environment into, each connected MCP server. ENDPOINT must inventory MCP servers configured per Codex install as distinct connection entities, capture each server's auth mode (OAuth vs. stdio `--env` secrets) and its scoped environment, and recognize that **read-only MCP tools now execute concurrently** — changing the per-server tool-execution timing model. New toxic combination: a Codex install with an OAuth-authenticated MCP server whose granted scopes exceed the task's need, or a per-server env carrying long-lived credentials

findings.title: Google Vertex AI — Colab Enterprise Data Science Agent (GA)
findings.description: A new code-executing agent entity now generally available inside Colab Enterprise notebooks. It autonomously plans, writes and **runs code**, and drives ML/forecasting and large-scale BigQuery ML / BigQuery DataFrames / Apache Spark jobs against uploaded CSVs or referenced BigQuery tables. AISPM (secondary tier) must add the Data Science Agent as a discoverable agent inventory entity per Colab Enterprise runtime, map its data reach (which BigQuery tables/datasets and uploaded files a given notebook agent can touch), and treat the notebook runtime + its IAM identity as the agent's blast-radius scope. Because the agent executes generated code with the notebook's data-access permissions, a prompt-injection or mis-scoped runtime identity becomes a path to autonomous reads/writes against connected BigQuery data — a new unmonitored data-flow for a secondary-tier platform

findings.title: Cursor — /loop Skill (scheduled unattended agent execution)
findings.description: Cursor v3.5 ships a bundled `/loop` skill that re-runs an agent prompt on a recurring local schedule until a target outcome is reached. This breaks the assumption that a Cursor agent only acts when a human is driving it: an agent can now persist and re-execute unattended on the endpoint. ENDPOINT (watching tier) should treat each active loop as a durable scheduled-task inventory entity (interval/cron, target prompt, terminating condition), attribute its repeated tool/command executions to the schedule rather than to a live user session, and flag loops that run privileged actions (deploys, external calls) without a human in the loop

platforms.name: Cursor
details: **Shared Canvases (Version 3.5, May 20, 2026)**: New external sharing surface for agent-produced interactive artifacts. Teams share dashboards and reports created by Cursor agents via browser links with read-only access — agent output now reaches users outside the IDE/Cursor account boundary for the first time. Source: https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/canvas

**Cursor Automations integration into Agents Window + multi-repo / standalone configurations (May 20, 2026)**: Automations now live inside the Agents Window. Supports multi-repository configurations and standalone setups (no repository required). Five new templates ship out of the box: Slack digest, analytics, FAQ, finance, customer health monitoring. Source: https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/automations

findings.title: Cursor — Shared Canvases (v3.5)
findings.description: Cursor agents can now produce interactive artifacts (dashboards, reports) that are externally shareable via browser links with read-only access. This creates a new outbound data-flow surface — agent output crosses the Cursor tenant boundary to non-Cursor recipients. Introduces new inventory entities: shared-canvas artifacts, share-link tokens, and external-reader identities. AISPM must discover Shared Canvas instances per workspace, map which agents are authorized to publish externally, and flag toxic combinations such as a canvas containing source-derived data being shared to an unauthenticated browser link

findings.title: Cursor — Automations multi-repo / standalone & expanded template surface
findings.description: Cursor Automations are now first-class Agents Window citizens, can operate across multiple repositories in one automation, and can run standalone (no repo at all). Five new templates (Slack digest, analytics, FAQ, finance, customer health monitoring) expand the kinds of business workflows automations execute. AISPM should treat each Automation as an inventory entity with a defined repo-set scope, recognize standalone automations as a distinct class (no repo-bounded blast radius), and add the new template types to the catalog so any standardized template instance can be discovered and audited

platforms.name: Amazon Q Developer
details: **Amazon Q artifacts (preview) — May 21, 2026**: New Q Developer capability that delivers responses enriched with table and chart visualizations *and* executes cross-service jobs in the AWS Management Console. Example: "Connect EC2 instance to an S3 bucket" returns a Q artifact that **grants permissions on the EC2 instance profile** and **makes bucket policy changes**. Supported services include EC2, RDS, Lambda, S3. All visualization data is persisted in **us-east-1** regardless of the source region. AmazonQFullAccess and AmazonQDeveloperAccess managed policies updated with `q:CreateArtifact`, `q:GetArtifact`, `q:GetArtifactActionResult`, `q:PerformArtifactAction`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/chat-artifacts.html

platforms.name: OpenAI Codex
details: **Codex 26.519 — Appshots (macOS), May 21, 2026**: New macOS-only capture mechanism — pressing both Command keys sends the frontmost application window to Codex with a screenshot. The capture pulls **text the app exposes including content outside the visible scroll area** into the thread as an attachment. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

**Codex 26.519 — Goal Mode GA, May 21, 2026**: Goal Mode promoted from experimental to GA. Codex now accepts a multi-hour objective and runs it autonomously **across session breaks, token-budget resets, and interruptions**. Live in the Codex app, VS Code and JetBrains extensions, and CLI 0.128.0+. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

**Codex 26.519 — Remote Computer Use, May 21, 2026**: New capability lets Codex drive desktop applications after the device is locked, via Codex Mobile from a smartphone. Safety controls include time-bound authorization, covered-screen behavior, automatic relock on first local input, and manual unlock fallback. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

**Codex Plugin Sharing — May 21, 2026**: ChatGPT Business teams can distribute **reusable plugin bundles** through marketplace sources. Discovery is "marketplace-aware" with remote collection support. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

**Codex CLI 0.133.0 — May 21, 2026**: Permission profiles expanded with **list APIs, inheritance support, and Windows sandbox integration**. `codex remote-control` operates as a foreground command. Extensions expose new lifecycle events including subagent transitions and tool execution. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
details: **AgentCore Runtime — bring-your-own file system, May 6, 2026**: New AgentCore Runtime capability that lets developers attach **Amazon S3 Files** and **Amazon EFS access points** directly to agent runtimes. The file system is **mounted into every session at a developer-specified path**, and agents read/write using standard POSIX-style file operations — "no custom mount code, no privileged containers, no download orchestration before the agent can start working." Sub-millisecond latency for active data, NFS close-to-open consistency. Multiple sessions/agents can share the same file system simultaneously, persisting intermediate results across sessions. Requires VPC configuration + access point ARN. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-filesystem-configurations.html

platforms.name: Anthropic — Project Glasswing
details: **Project Glasswing: Initial update — May 22, 2026**: Anthropic published its first results update for Project Glasswing (the cybersecurity initiative powered by Claude Mythos Preview, originally introduced April 7, 2026). Mythos Preview has now uncovered **10,000+ high/critical-severity vulnerabilities** across widely used software systems via a coalition of ~50 trusted partners. **Cloudflare** (~2,000 bugs, 400 H/C-severity — fewer false positives than human testers), **Mozilla** (271 vulnerabilities fixed in Firefox 150, 10× more than older Claude models), and **Verizon** (joined May 2026) are confirmed partners. Open-source program scanned 1,000+ projects, found 6,202 H/C-severity vulnerabilities (90.6% confirmed legitimate true positives, 62.4% validated as H/C-severity). Expansion plan includes **U.S. and allied governments**. Anthropic states: "no company — including itself — has yet developed safeguards reliable enough to prevent the malicious use of models with Mythos-level capabilities." Source: https://www.anthropic.com/research/glasswing-initial-update

findings.title: Amazon Q Developer artifacts (preview) — Q can perform cross-service AWS actions
findings.description: Brand-new capability that promotes Amazon Q from a chat surface to an **action-executing agent in the AWS Management Console**. Introduces three new inventory entities: **Q artifact** (the response payload), **Q artifact action** (the cross-service job, e.g., grant S3 bucket policy + modify EC2 instance profile), and **Q artifact action result**. New IAM actions `q:CreateArtifact`, `q:GetArtifact`, `q:GetArtifactActionResult`, `q:PerformArtifactAction` are now baked into the **AmazonQFullAccess** and **AmazonQDeveloperAccess** managed policies, so every principal granted these policies inherits artifact-action capability transitively. AISPM must inventory which IAM principals carry these permissions, treat Q artifacts as a new high-privilege agent-tool primitive (cross-service mutations on EC2/RDS/Lambda/S3 from a chat prompt), and surface us-east-1 visualization data as a new data-residency signal. New toxic combination: overprivileged IAM principal + Q artifact action permissions + sensitive workload (production, regulated)

findings.title: Amazon Q Developer artifacts — prompt-injection-driven AWS resource mutation
findings.description: New attack surface. A prompt-injection that reaches Amazon Q in the AWS console can trigger `q:PerformArtifactAction` to mutate live infrastructure (e.g., bucket policies, instance-profile permissions). AIRT should add automated tests for prompt-injection-to-artifact-action chains, artifact action authorization bypasses, and unexpected cross-service writes initiated through Q

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — Appshots (macOS screen + non-visible text exfiltration vector)
findings.description: Codex now ingests the frontmost macOS window's screenshot **plus any text the app exposes, including content outside the visible scroll area**, via a double-Command-key shortcut. This is a new endpoint data-egress channel — a Codex agent prompt can now reference contents of any window the user surfaces (Slack threads, password managers, email drafts, CRM records). ENDPOINT must add Appshots as a Codex local data primitive, recognize Mac-windowed apps as a per-window inventory class, and flag double-Command captures in sensitive apps

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — Goal Mode GA (multi-hour autonomous objective execution)
findings.description: Goal Mode promoted to GA. Codex now runs **multi-hour autonomous objectives** that persist across session breaks, token-budget resets, and interruptions, live in the app, VS Code, JetBrains, and CLI. ENDPOINT must treat each Goal as a distinct durable session resource (not a one-shot prompt), inventory active Goals per user, and track which IDE extension and CLI version is hosting each Goal. New telemetry class: Goal lifecycle events (start, pause, resume, complete) and the persistent objective text

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — Remote Computer Use (locked-Mac control from Codex Mobile)
findings.description: First time Codex agency persists past the screen lock. From a smartphone via Codex Mobile, Codex can drive desktop apps **even when the Mac is locked and screen off**. ENDPOINT must add Remote Computer Use sessions as a new endpoint class with mobile-initiated authorization, treat the time-bound authorization window as a discrete inventory event, and capture every Remote Computer Use session boundary (relock, manual unlock, screen cover). This breaks the assumption "if the device is locked, the agent is idle."

findings.title: OpenAI Codex Plugin Sharing — marketplace plugin bundles for ChatGPT Business
findings.description: New distribution channel — ChatGPT Business teams can publish and share **plugin bundles** discoverable through marketplace sources. Plugin discovery is now "marketplace-aware with remote collection support." ENDPOINT/AISPM must inventory plugins by source (first-party vs. marketplace bundle), track which teams have published vs. installed which bundles, and treat the plugin-bundle ID as a new resource type that propagates between users. New supply-chain inventory entity

findings.title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.133.0 — Windows sandbox integration + permission profile inheritance
findings.description: Codex CLI 0.133.0 adds **Windows sandbox integration** (previously macOS/Linux only) and **permission profile inheritance** with list APIs. ENDPOINT must extend the Codex CLI inventory to Windows hosts, treat Windows sandbox-bounded Codex sessions as a new class, and reconcile inherited permission profiles into the effective-permissions graph (a child profile may relax constraints set by its parent)

findings.title: AgentCore Runtime — bring-your-own file system (S3 / EFS mounted into agent sessions)
findings.description: New AgentCore Runtime capability that mounts **Amazon S3 Files and Amazon EFS access points directly into every agent session at a developer-specified path**. Each agent now has POSIX-style read/write access to potentially large enterprise data stores without custom mount code or privileged containers. Multiple sessions/agents can share the same file system simultaneously. AISPM must inventory the access-point ARNs attached to each AgentCore Runtime, map the data-store blast radius per agent (which S3/EFS access points an agent can read or write), and treat the VPC + access-point ARN tuple as a new agent-environment inventory class. New toxic combination: overprivileged agent + writable EFS access point + cross-team data store

findings.title: AgentCore Runtime — file-system data flows for S3 Files / EFS
findings.description: BYO file system adds an entirely new data-flow class to AgentCore agents — sustained POSIX file I/O against enterprise stores, distinct from API-call or Gateway-routed traffic. AIDR must add a file-system-IO activity stream per AgentCore session, with read/write attribution and access-point-scoped data-flow accounting (e.g., "agent X wrote 4 GB to EFS access point Y during session Z")

findings.title: Anthropic Project Glasswing — Mythos Preview expansion to OSS + critical infrastructure partners
findings.description: Project Glasswing partner expansion (Cloudflare, Mozilla, Verizon, US/allied governments) and OSS scanning at scale (1,000+ projects, 6,202 H/C-severity vulnerabilities found, 90.6% true-positive rate) confirm that **Claude Mythos Preview is now operating as a multi-partner vulnerability-discovery agent on critical software**. AIRT should add Mythos-Preview-class agents as a distinct adversarial test profile (Mythos has higher cybersecurity-vulnerability-discovery capability than other Claude variants), and track which Anthropic deployments are running under Project Glasswing allowlist. Public reporting of partner roster expands the set of attack scenarios Zenity should rehearse against

platforms.name: Microsoft Agent 365 (new product surface)
details: **Microsoft Agent 365 — GA May 1, 2026**: New per-user-licensed Microsoft product ($15/user/mo, Commercial segment) for observing, governing, and securing AI agents. Three pillars — **Observe** (Agent registry, Registry sync, Agent Map showing all agents in a single centralized registry in the M365 admin center), **Govern** (lifecycle management, access control, compliance through M365 admin center + Microsoft Entra + Microsoft Purview), **Secure** (Entra Conditional Access for agents, Purview DLP/info-protection, Defender real-time runtime protection). At launch, a set of **pre-integrated ecosystem partner agents** are deployable directly from the M365 admin center. Source: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/01/microsoft-agent-365-now-generally-available-expands-capabilities-and-integrations/

**Agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center**: New centralized agent inventory surface in the M365 admin center, with **Registry sync** to pull external agent inventory and **Agent Map** for visualization. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/agent-registry

**Microsoft Defender — real-time agent protection during runtime**: New Defender feature blocks unsafe behaviors and malicious activity for agents at runtime. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/real-time-agent-protection-during-runtime

**Microsoft Purview — AI agent governance for Agent 365**: New Purview surface for managing data security and compliance for Agent-365-registered agents. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/ai-agent-365

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
details: **AgentCore Payments (preview)**: New managed service enabling microtransaction payments for AI agents using the **x402 protocol**. Wallet integration with **Coinbase CDP** and **Stripe (Privy)**. Built-in budget controls per `PaymentSession` (configurable `maxSpendAmount`, currency, expiry). Pre-integrated **Coinbase x402 Bazaar MCP server** exposing 10,000+ pay-per-use x402 endpoints via AgentCore Gateway. New API surface: `CreatePaymentInstrument`, `CreatePaymentSession`, `ProcessPayment`, `GetPaymentInstrumentBalance`, `GetResourcePaymentToken`, plus a new `PaymentCredentialProvider` resource stored in AgentCore Identity. Available in us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-2. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/payments.html

**AgentCore Harness (preview)**: New managed agent harness/loop powered by **Strands Agents** (AWS's open-source agent framework). Each session runs in **isolated microVM** with its own filesystem and shell. Persistent short-term and long-term memory across sessions; **mid-session model switching** (Bedrock, OpenAI, Google Gemini). BYO custom container environment. Harness config exports to Strands Agents code. Available in us-west-2, us-east-1, ap-southeast-2, eu-central-1. New API: `InvokeHarness`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness.html

**AgentCore Registry**: New centralized catalog for agents, MCP servers, tools, skills, and custom resources across an organization. Provides governed publish/review/approve workflow with hybrid semantic + keyword search. New API: `SearchRegistryRecords`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/registry.html

**AgentCore Policy**: Cedar-based deterministic policy controls (in addition to natural-language rules) that intercept every tool call in AgentCore Gateway before execution. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/policy.html

**AgentCore Evaluations — A/B testing APIs**: New `CreateABTest`/`GetABTest`/`UpdateABTest`/`DeleteABTest`/`ListABTests` APIs alongside `StartBatchEvaluation`/`GetBatchEvaluation` for purpose-built evaluations across sessions/traces/spans. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/evaluations.html

platforms.name: Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI
details: **GPT Realtime Translate (preview, May 2026)**: New realtime model for continuous stream-based audio translation for live multilingual events, customer support, and voice assistants. Same `/realtime` endpoint surface. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry-classic/openai/concepts/gpt-realtime-translate

**GPT Realtime Whisper (preview, May 2026)**: New low-latency streaming transcription model for live captions, monitoring, and archival workflows. Same `/realtime` endpoint surface. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry-classic/openai/concepts/gpt-realtime-whisper

platforms.name: Cursor
details: **Cursor Automations 2.0 (May 20, 2026)**: Major expansion. Automations now live in the **Agents Window** workspace (previously cursor.com/automations only). New **multi-repository support** — a single automation can attach multiple repos, allowing the cloud agent context to span codebases; Dockerfile-based environment configuration with build-secrets support for private package registries. New **no-repository automations** — automations can run without any repo attached, for operational/non-code tasks. Five new marketplace templates: **Slack digest agent**, **product analytics agent**, **product FAQ agent**, **product finance agent**, **customer health monitoring agent**. Source: https://forum.cursor.com/t/improvements-to-cursor-automations/161149

platforms.name: Perplexity
details: **finance_search tool in Agent API (May 2026)**: New tool added to the Perplexity `/v1/agent` endpoint for structured financial and market data — quotes, financials, earnings, analyst estimates, segment KPIs, ETF constituents, insider activity, market movers, ETF constituents, index details. Joins the existing tool set: `web_search`, `people_search`, `fetch_url`, function tools. Billed at $5 per 1,000 invocations (model tokens billed separately). Source: https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/agent-api/finance-search

platforms.name: Salesforce AgentForce
details: **"Topics" renamed to "Subagents" (April 2026)**: AgentForce agent **topics** have been renamed to **subagents** organization-wide in the developer documentation to better reflect their role as specialized agents with specific expertise. No functional change, but documentation transitions both terms during migration. Source: https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2026/05/new-agentforce-metadata-and-development-lifecycle

findings.title: Microsoft Agent 365 — observe/govern/secure control plane GA
findings.description: New Microsoft product (GA May 1, 2026, $15/user/mo) that is a direct competitor surface to Zenity AISPM. Introduces a centralized **Agent registry** in the M365 admin center, **Registry sync** (pulls external agent inventories), and an **Agent Map** for visualization — plus tight integrations with Entra (agent identity, Conditional Access for agents), Purview (DLP, AI agent risk), and Defender (real-time runtime protection). Pre-integrated ecosystem partner agents deploy directly from the admin center. AISPM must track tenants enabling Agent 365 as a distinct governance class, reconcile Agent 365 inventory against Zenity's, and recognize Agent-365-registered agents as an inventory-source-of-truth signal. AIDR should detect when Defender's real-time-agent-protection blocks an action and treat it as a coverage handoff

findings.title: AgentCore Payments — agent-driven microtransactions over x402 protocol
findings.description: Brand-new AgentCore service (preview) that lets agents autonomously spend money. Introduces multiple new inventory entities: `PaymentInstrument`, `PaymentSession` (with `maxSpendAmount`, currency, expiry), and `PaymentCredentialProvider` (wallet creds for Coinbase CDP and Stripe-Privy stored in AgentCore Identity). Wires in 10,000+ third-party paid endpoints via the pre-integrated **Coinbase x402 Bazaar MCP server** through AgentCore Gateway. AISPM must inventory each agent's payment instruments, sessions, and budget caps; new toxic-combination class: overprivileged agent + active PaymentSession + unrestricted Gateway target

findings.title: AgentCore Payments — payment data flow + spending observability
findings.description: Each payment flow emits CloudWatch vended logs + X-Ray vended spans for every data-plane API call. AIDR gains an entirely new activity-type stream — payment requests, x402 challenge responses, wallet-signing events, budget-deduction events, failed-signing exceptions — and a new detection surface for runaway agent spending

findings.title: AgentCore Payments — x402 + crypto-wallet attack surface
findings.description: Three distinct new attack surfaces: (a) `PaymentSession` budget bypass via session reuse or expiry races, (b) wallet credential exfil from `PaymentCredentialProvider` (Coinbase API keys, Stripe-Privy secrets) stored in AgentCore Identity, (c) malicious x402-Bazaar MCP endpoints draining agent budgets through inflated micro-charges or fee inflation. AIRT should add automated tests for x402 payment-required flow tampering, budget-cap evasion, and prompt-injection-driven payment authorization

findings.title: AgentCore Harness — managed agent-loop runtime with microVM sessions
findings.description: New preview service replacing the bespoke agent harness with a managed loop powered by Strands Agents. Each session runs in an isolated microVM with filesystem and shell access, persistent short-term + long-term memory across sessions, and **mid-session model switching** (Bedrock, OpenAI, Gemini). New API `InvokeHarness` and a distinct session resource class. Harness config can be exported to Strands Agents code. AISPM must inventory Harness sessions per agent, capture the model-provider trail across mid-session swaps, and treat BYO container images as a custom-environment inventory class

findings.title: AgentCore Registry — central agent/tool/MCP-server catalog
findings.description: New AgentCore service that catalogs every agent, MCP server, tool, skill, and custom resource across an organization with governed publish/review/approve workflows and hybrid semantic+keyword search. Functions as a customer-side AISPM signal source — Zenity can reconcile its inventory against Registry entries, and Registry's approval state becomes a new policy attribute (approved vs unapproved tool, deployed where). New API `SearchRegistryRecords`

findings.title: AgentCore Policy — Cedar-based pre-execution policy enforcement
findings.description: AgentCore Policy now exposes Cedar (AWS's open-source policy language) in addition to natural-language rules, and intercepts every tool call in AgentCore Gateway before execution. New policy resource class with deterministic rule semantics that AISPM should treat as authoritative for tool-execution authorization decisions

findings.title: AgentCore Evaluations — A/B testing APIs
findings.description: New `CreateABTest`/`UpdateABTest`/`DeleteABTest`/`ListABTests` plus `StartBatchEvaluation`/`StopBatchEvaluation` APIs extend evaluation from sessions/traces/spans into A/B test resources. New `ABTest` inventory class with associated batch evaluation runs; AISPM should map ABTest → agent variants → traffic-split signals

findings.title: Azure OpenAI — GPT Realtime Translate (live multilingual audio streaming)
findings.description: New realtime model dedicated to continuous stream-based audio translation. Same `/realtime` endpoint as other realtime models, but introduces a translation-specific data flow — source-language audio in, target-language audio out — for live multilingual events, customer support, and voice assistants. New AIDR signal class: cross-language audio-to-audio session, where source and target language attributes need separate tracking

findings.title: Azure OpenAI — GPT Realtime Whisper (low-latency streaming transcription)
findings.description: New realtime ASR model for live captions, monitoring, and archival workflows on the `/realtime` endpoint. Distinct from prior `gpt-4o-transcribe-*` chains in that transcription is now a first-class realtime modality. AIDR gains a streaming-transcript activity type for archival and monitoring traffic categories

findings.title: Cursor — Automations 2.0 (multi-repo, no-repo, marketplace templates)
findings.description: Cursor Automations expand beyond the standalone web UI into the Agents Window. Three new endpoint sub-classes: (a) **multi-repo automations** — one automation spans multiple attached repos, breaking the 1:1 repo↔agent assumption; (b) **no-repository automations** — operational tasks (e.g. Slack digest, customer-health monitoring) without any code surface, which extends Cursor as a general-purpose autonomous agent platform rather than just a coding agent; (c) **marketplace templates** as a discoverable distribution channel for shared automation patterns (Slack digest, product analytics, FAQ, finance, customer-health agents). ENDPOINT must update the Cursor inventory model to treat automations as a distinct endpoint class with N-repo or zero-repo binding; AISPM should map automation → triggered cloud-agent runs → connected data sources

findings.title: Perplexity — finance_search tool in Agent API
findings.description: New `finance_search` tool added to the Perplexity Agent API (`POST /v1/agent`) for structured financial/market data — quotes, financials, earnings, analyst estimates, segment KPIs, ETF constituents, insider activity, market movers. Joins `web_search`, `people_search`, `fetch_url`, and function tools. Billed at $5 per 1,000 invocations. AISPM must add `finance_search` as a Perplexity-agent tool primitive and recognize it as a finance-data egress channel; this is a different sensitivity class than `web_search`

findings.title: Salesforce AgentForce — "Topics" renamed to "Subagents"
findings.description: AgentForce agent **topics** were renamed to **subagents** in the developer documentation in April 2026 — no functional change, but the new noun signals a shift in inventory mental model (topic-as-scoped-instruction-block → subagent-as-named-actor) reflecting their specialized-expert positioning. AISPM should rename the AgentForce topic primitive to subagent across the Salesforce inventory schema and watch for downstream API renames that may follow

platforms.name: Anthropic (Claude Enterprise)
details: **Anthropic acquires Stainless (May 18, 2026)**: $300M+ acquisition of the SDK-generation startup whose tooling powers every official Anthropic SDK and is also used by OpenAI, Google, Cloudflare. Hosted Stainless products (including the SDK generator) will be wound down. Strategic intent is to control SDK and MCP-server tooling for the AI agent ecosystem. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-acquires-stainless

**KPMG Strategic Alliance + KPMG Digital Gateway Powered by Claude (May 19, 2026)**: Global alliance deploying Claude to 276,000+ KPMG employees worldwide. Claude is embedded inside KPMG Digital Gateway — KPMG's client-delivery platform — starting with new tools for tax and legal clients. KPMG is also named Anthropic's preferred PE partner; joint Claude-powered products for PE portfolio companies are planned. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-kpmg

platforms.name: OpenAI Codex
details: **Codex CLI 0.132.0 (May 20, 2026)**: Python SDK authentication expansion — API key login, ChatGPT browser flow, device-code flows. Text-based workflows now accept plain string inputs; resumed automations retain session context with structured output. Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.132.0

**Codex CLI 0.131.0 (May 18, 2026)**: Unified `@` mentions across files, directories, plugins, and skills. Plugin marketplace CLI commands with version-aware sharing, share checkout, clearer shared-workspace buckets, and default-enabled plugin hooks. Remote environments now support a daemon-managed `codex remote-control`, with runtime enable/disable APIs, status reads, and registry-backed configuration. Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.131.0

platforms.name: Cursor
details: **Cursor in Jira (May 19, 2026)**: New integration. Jira work items can be assigned directly to cloud agents, or users can `@Cursor` mention in Jira comments. The system pulls ticket context to scope the task and opens a pull request when complete. Source: https://cursor.com/docs/integrations/jira

**Composer 2.5 (May 18, 2026)**: New Cursor in-house coding model built on the Kimi K2.5 base from Moonshot AI, with 85% of compute spent on Cursor's RL/post-training. Matches Claude Opus 4.7 on key coding benchmarks at ~1/10 the cost; trained on 25× more synthetic coding tasks than Composer 2. Pricing: Standard $0.50/$2.50 per M input/output tokens; Fast (default) $3.00/$15.00. Source: https://cursor.com/blog/composer-2-5

platforms.name: ServiceNow
details: **AI Control Tower expansion (Australia release, GA expected Aug 2026; Innovation Lab in May 2026)**: AI Control Tower now operates across five areas — discovery, observation, governance, security, and measurement — and adds 30 new enterprise connectors that reach beyond ServiceNow into AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, SAP, Oracle, and Workday. Adds enforcement / agent kill-switch capabilities. Source: https://newsroom.servicenow.com/press-releases/details/2026/ServiceNow-expands-AI-Control-Tower-to-discover-observe-govern-secure-and-measure-AI-deployed-across-any-system-in-the-enterprise/default.aspx

**Project Arc — autonomous desktop agent (Australia release, May 2026)**: New ServiceNow autonomous desktop agent that resides on employee desktops and completes work autonomously. Secured by Nvidia OpenShell runtime; governed by ServiceNow AI Control Tower. Source: https://www.servicenow.com/products/ai-control-tower.html

platforms.name: Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI
details: **GPT Realtime 2.0 (preview, May 2026)**: New speech-to-speech model with built-in reasoning. Adjustable `reasoning.effort` (minimal/low/medium/high), response phases distinguishing preambles ("commentary") from final answers ("final_answer"), and an extended 256K-token context window. Same connection/usage patterns as earlier realtime models. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/realtime-2

findings.title: Anthropic — Stainless acquisition + hosted-SDK-tooling shutdown
findings.description: Anthropic acquired the SDK-generation infrastructure used by every official Anthropic library — and also by OpenAI, Google, and Cloudflare. Hosted Stainless products (SDK generator, MCP-related tooling) will be wound down. This collapses three vendors' SDKs onto a single owner-controlled toolchain, and meaningfully shifts where MCP-server scaffolding is generated. AISPM must register that customer-side SDK regeneration workflows will move; for Claude-enterprise customers, the official SDK inventory class now derives from Anthropic-owned tooling end-to-end. Watch for surfacing of Anthropic-built MCP/SDK templates as new agent inventory primitives

findings.title: Anthropic — KPMG Digital Gateway Powered by Claude
findings.description: New named product (Digital Gateway Powered by Claude) embedded into KPMG's client-delivery platform, rolled out to 276,000+ KPMG employees plus client-facing tax and legal workflows. Introduces a new deployment class — Claude inside a Big-4 consultancy's client-delivery product — where the consultancy mediates Claude access to client data. AISPM should treat Digital Gateway-Claude tenants as a distinct inventory class with consultancy-mediated identity and data flows, and recognize PE portfolio company sub-tenants as a downstream sharing surface

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — daemon-managed remote-control + registry-backed remote environments (CLI 0.131)
findings.description: New class of Codex endpoint: a long-running, daemon-controlled `codex remote-control` server with runtime enable/disable APIs, status reads, and a backing registry for environment configuration. This creates a new persistent-daemon endpoint class distinct from the CLI/desktop/Chrome/mobile classes, callable headlessly across multiple environments via `view_image` and other multi-environment resolutions. ENDPOINT must enumerate hosts running the Codex daemon and discover registry-backed environments; AISPM should map per-environment policy state (enabled vs disabled, registry source)

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — plugin marketplace CLI commands
findings.description: First-class CLI tooling for installing, version-pinning, and sharing plugins through a marketplace, with default-enabled plugin hooks and shared-workspace bucket semantics. Extends the Codex plugin marketplace (already in the May 18 report) with a CLI-managed distribution path. ENDPOINT/AISPM inventory of installed plugins should now include CLI-installed plugins with version pins, share-checkout origin, and hook-enabled state

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — Python SDK expanded auth flows (API key, ChatGPT-browser, device-code)
findings.description: Codex CLI 0.132 expands authentication into Python SDK contexts with three new flows: API key login, ChatGPT browser auth flow, and device-code flow. Each opens new attack surface — device-code phishing, browser-flow session hijack, and SDK-resident API-key exfil. AIRT should add tests for device-code phishing into Codex sessions and for replay of SDK-resident auth artifacts

findings.title: Cursor — Jira integration (Cursor in Jira)
findings.description: Cursor cloud agents are now invokable from Jira via direct work-item assignment or `@Cursor` mentions in comments; ticket context auto-scopes the agent's task and a PR is opened on completion. New embedded endpoint class — Jira-driven cloud agent — that bypasses the IDE and the Teams channel surface previously reported. ENDPOINT must recognize Jira-driven Cursor invocations as a distinct endpoint and capture the ticket → cloud-agent → PR data flow; AISPM should treat the Jira-Cursor binding as an authorization edge (any Jira user can drive a code change)

findings.title: Cursor — Composer 2.5 in-house model
findings.description: New Cursor-owned coding model derived from Kimi K2.5 (Moonshot AI), with claimed parity to Claude Opus 4.7 on coding benchmarks at ~1/10 the cost. Introduces a new model SKU served from Cursor's own infra (rather than routed to a third-party provider), with two pricing tiers (Standard / Fast). AISPM must add Composer 2.5 to the model inventory for Cursor agents and recognize the Cursor-served path as a distinct data-flow channel (no third-party LLM hop)

findings.title: ServiceNow — AI Control Tower cross-platform expansion (AWS/GCP/Azure/SAP/Oracle/Workday connectors)
findings.description: AI Control Tower expands from ServiceNow-only AI governance to a cross-platform discovery / observation / governance / security / measurement surface with 30 new enterprise connectors spanning the three hyperscalers and SAP/Oracle/Workday. Adds enforcement controls including agent kill switches. This makes AI Control Tower a direct competitor surface to Zenity AISPM — and a new inventory source if Zenity ever consumes its findings. AISPM should at minimum track tenants enabling AI Control Tower cross-platform mode and reconcile its inventory against Zenity's

findings.title: ServiceNow — Project Arc autonomous desktop agent
findings.description: New ServiceNow autonomous desktop agent that resides on employee desktops and executes work autonomously, secured by Nvidia OpenShell runtime and governed by ServiceNow AI Control Tower. Introduces an entirely new local-AI endpoint class for ServiceNow (previously Now Assist was a hosted chat agent only). ENDPOINT must inventory Project Arc installs as a distinct endpoint class with desktop-execution scope and OpenShell-runtime containment; AISPM should map Project Arc agents to the AI Control Tower governance edge

findings.title: Azure OpenAI — GPT Realtime 2.0 (reasoning-in-realtime, 256K context)
findings.description: Speech-to-speech model with built-in reasoning, configurable `reasoning.effort` control (minimal/low/medium/high), response phases distinguishing preambles from final answers, and 256K-token context. Same realtime endpoint surface as earlier models. New AIDR signal types: preamble vs final_answer in the response stream, plus `reasoning.effort`-tagged sessions; new AISPM model SKU for Azure-OpenAI agent inventory. Voice-modality content can now carry multi-step reasoning chains that previously required text-pipeline routing
